facts.VIEW-MANDATE: **Mandate ledger:** every owner request, ruling, constraint and accepted discovered obligation, with a stable id and source.
facts.VIEW-ROUTE: **Epic route:** the complete hierarchy and dependency graph from current state to closure, including all distant stages at least as named summary nodes.
facts.VIEW-FRONTIER: **Expanded frontier:** the current branch of the hierarchy plus the next risk/dependency boundary, decomposed into reviewable atoms.
facts.VIEW-ATOM: **Current atom contract:** input, write perimeter, acceptance, minimum sufficient affected verification with target and expected cases, evidence and safe-stop condition. Refresh the verification recipe after the real diff. A counterfactual mutation diagnostic appears only when the suspicion and economy conditions in @spec://org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning/flows/multi-user-planning/campaign-execution#MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW are met.
facts.VIEW-PROJECTION: **Linear projection:** the small list shown by a harness UI. It is derived navigation, never storage and never proof that omitted descendants do not exist.

format.title: 2. `plan.toml` reference format

p.PLAN-FORMAT: `plan.toml` is strict, human-authored local TOML, replaced atomically after each accepted plan mutation. `revision` increases monotonically. Stable ids are never reused.

format.fence:
schema = 1 plan_id = "compiler-modernization" revision = 42 root_node = "ROOT" current_node = "COMPILER-4.1" updated_at = "2026-08-29T11:00:00Z"
[[mandate]] id = "M-017" source = "owner-chat:2026-08-29" text = "A handoff must preserve unaccepted compiler work as candidate." disposition = "owned" nodes = ["COMPILER-4.1", "HANDOFF-1"]
[[node]] id = "COMPILER-4.1" parent = "COMPILER-4" order = 60 kind = "atom" title = "Execute the compiler transform schedule" state = "candidate" zoom = "expanded" depends_on = ["COMPILER-4.0"] completes_after = ["COMPILER-4.2"] mandates = ["M-017"] acceptance = ["review complete diff", "run exact affected tests"] evidence = ["repo:reports/compiler-transform-candidate.md"]

p.MANDATE-DISPOSITIONS: Mandate disposition is one of `owned | accepted | deferred | duplicate | superseded | declined | out-of-scope`. Every value except `owned` and `accepted` carries a reason; `declined` and `out-of-scope` require owner authority. Deferral names its future home or trigger.

p.NODE-STATES: Leaf state is one of `planned | ready | active | candidate | accepted | blocked | deferred | dropped | superseded`. `candidate` means implementation exists but central acceptance is open. Parents close bottom-up: a parent cannot be `accepted` while a required descendant is non-terminal, while one of its own `completes_after` gates is non-terminal, or while its own exit evidence is absent.

p.START-GATE-INHERITED: `depends_on` is a **start** gate and is inherited: a node cannot start before its own and every ancestor's `depends_on` targets are terminal. This is unchanged, so every plan written before completion gates existed keeps its exact meaning.

p.COMPLETION-GATES: **`completes_after`** is an optional per-node string array of node ids and a **completion** gate for that node alone. The node cannot become `accepted` while any listed node is non-terminal. It is **not inherited**: it does not gate starting, dispatch or readiness of the node or of any descendant, and children may start and be accepted while the gate is still open. It exists because a parent can owe a final step of its own — a design that generalises what its children already delivered, a consolidation, a migration of the surface the children built — which is a prerequisite of closing that node, not a prerequisite of each child; expressing it as `depends_on` would wrongly stall every child. An absent field is no gate. Both edge kinds share one acyclicity check, because a start gate and a completion gate can deadlock each other, and an unknown id in either is an invalid plan. Acceptance of a gated node still needs its evidence, its terminal descendants and its inherited start gates. Owner decision 2026-11-10: «completes_after делай».

p.EXECUTION-COMPATIBILITY: Working windows, bounded worker packets, verification selection/reuse and interruption recovery are procedures over existing nodes. They do not introduce a second queue, new node states or required plan fields. Preserve stable ids, dependencies, dispositions, acceptance, evidence and campaign-specific extension fields. Derive a working packet from the complete plan; do not replace the plan with that packet.

p.VERIFICATION-REFINEMENT: Keep a concise claim-to-target/case selection note in existing packets and evidence, not new required plan fields. A coordinator may refine an overbroad command into proven narrower equivalents while retaining its affected acceptance obligations and recording the replacement. The designated comprehensive final gate remains owed. Canon: @spec://org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning/flows/multi-user-planning/verification-selection#root.

p.RECOVERY-EVIDENCE: When retries or effects need a durable record, use existing evidence references and ordinary local reports. Identify the node, input snapshot, completed/unknown effects, consumed attempts and next discriminating check. This is evidence about execution, not new authority or a compulsory session record; old plans remain usable without it. Missing evidence requires reconstruction, not invented completion.

p.COVERAGE-SKELETON: A campaign may begin before every distant atom is known, but never before every known obligation is represented. Unknown detail is a named refinement node with an explicit trigger and boundary, not an omitted region. The plan is complete in coverage and progressively precise in execution.

p.DEPENDENCIES-EXPLICIT: Every node that cannot start independently names `depends_on`, and every node that cannot close until another finishes names `completes_after`; resource, owner-decision and external-state gates are first-class nodes. A linear ordering must not hide a dependency graph.

p.ZOOM-RULE: Expand the current path, all candidate work awaiting acceptance, and enough successors to cross the next high-risk or irreversible boundary. Keep distant stages as summary nodes with exit criteria. Increase zoom when uncertainty, coupling, public surface or reversal cost rises; decrease it after evidence closes uncertainty.

p.ATOM-SHAPE: A reviewable atom has one coherent purpose, an explicit write perimeter, named affected verification and a safe stopping state. Plan the build/test target before an exact case or small family, including named contract consumers. Ordinary negative-case and invariant tests remain part of that essential floor; broad suites are not its default. Counterfactual mutation is optional diagnostic evidence only under @spec://org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning/flows/multi-user-planning/campaign-execution#MUTATION-DIAGNOSTIC-LAW. Atom size is determined by verification cost, not by a fixed line count.

p.REPLAN-TRIGGERS: Replan immediately when: the owner changes scope or supplies a ruling; evidence falsifies an assumption; a test or review reveals an omitted obligation; dependencies or resources change; a worker discovers architecture outside its atom; a custody handoff occurs; or the current route conflicts with a governing specification.

p.REPLAN-PROCEDURE: Record the new fact, trace affected mandate and nodes, preserve old node ids and dispositions, revise dependencies/zoom/acceptance, then regenerate the linear projection. Never rewrite history so the old route appears never to have existed; the changed decision and its reason remain reviewable.

p.PLAN-CANNOT-SELF-CLOSE: An empty ready queue or completed UI list cannot close a campaign. Closure requires all mandate items disposed, all required nodes terminal, acceptance evidence present, durable knowledge promoted, cleanup safety proven, and the campaign's exit gate run.

p.PROJECTION: The projection prioritizes: candidates awaiting central verdict; active atom; ready dependencies; then the next ordered child on each expanded frontier. It includes ancestor labels and a count of collapsed descendants. Ties use `order`, then stable id. Changing UI capacity changes only how many projected rows appear, never the plan.

p.NO-THREE-STEP-STOP: A coordinator presented with a three-row projection must read the authoritative plan before declaring scope or completion. “I finished the plan shown by the UI” is not a closure argument.

p.TREE-DISPLAY-BUCKETS: **Display buckets.** A viewer maps each node state onto exactly one display bucket: `accepted` → accepted; `candidate` → candidate; `active` → active; `ready` → ready; `planned` → planned; `blocked` → blocked; `deferred` → deferred; `dropped` and `superseded` → closed; any other value → unknown. `accepted` and `candidate` never share a bucket or a label: implemented and accepted are different facts, so a candidate is named as done-awaiting-acceptance and never as done. A closed bucket is named as closed without completion. An unknown value is reported as a validation warning naming the node, never displayed as a readiness the plan does not state. Buckets are presentation only: they add no node state, no ordering and no authority.

p.TREE-LEAF-COUNTING: **Counting rule.** Every per-parent count is taken over that parent's leaf descendants only. A leaf is a node with no children; it counts exactly once, in the bucket of its own state. A parent's own state is never counted in its own totals and no node is counted twice, so a parent's buckets always sum to its leaf-descendant total and the root totals equal the plan's leaf count. Collapsing, filtering and searching change what is displayed, never a count. Counts are arithmetic over states: they are not progress, not acceptance and not closure evidence.

p.TREE-VIEWER-IS-DERIVED: **A viewer is derived navigation.** A rendered tree is a projection like the linear projection above: it is written outside the plan, never read back as state, and introduces no node field, state or ordering of its own. It renders the verdict of this package's own plan validator, so a drawn tree cannot contradict the tools; nodes still render under a failing verdict, because an invalid plan is exactly what needs looking at. Dependencies are shown as typed edges, which lets a plan carry more than one dependency kind without changing this display law. Reference viewer: `spec://org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning/skills/steward-tree#root`.
